title: Total Alkalinity — Titration Method
reagents: Bromcresol green-methyl red or phenolphthalein indicator
steps: Measure 100 mL of sample (or a smaller aliquot diluted to 100 mL) into a flask.
If checking for phenolphthalein alkalinity, add 2-3 drops of phenolphthalein indicator; titrate with standard acid to a colorless endpoint (pH 8.3) and record volume as P.
Add 2-3 drops of bromcresol green-methyl red indicator (or continue monitoring with a pH meter).
Titrate with standard acid to the pH 4.5 endpoint (color changes from blue-green to a light pink/red, or pH meter reads 4.5).
Record total titrant volume used as the total alkalinity titration volume.
Calculate mg/L as CaCO3 using the Total Alkalinity calculator.
safetyNotes: Acid handling — wear safety glasses and gloves.
Rinse burette and glassware with distilled water between samples.

title: Total, Calcium, and Magnesium Hardness — EDTA Titration
steps: For total hardness: measure 100 mL sample, add ~2 mL pH 10 buffer, add a small amount of Eriochrome Black T indicator.
Titrate with EDTA titrant until the color changes from wine-red to blue; record titrant volume.
For calcium hardness: measure a fresh 100 mL sample, add 1N NaOH to raise pH to 12-13, add murexide indicator.
Titrate with EDTA until the color changes from pink to purple; record titrant volume.
Calculate total, calcium, and magnesium hardness (by difference) using the Hardness calculator.
safetyNotes: NaOH is caustic — wear gloves and eye protection.

title: Chlorine Residual — DPD Colorimetric Method
steps: Rinse the sample cell with sample water.
Fill the sample cell to the fill line with sample.
Add the DPD reagent, cap, and invert gently to mix (do not shake vigorously).
Read the result within 1 minute on the colorimeter (color fades over time).
If the sample was diluted to fit the instrument's range, apply the dilution factor using the Chlorine Residual calculator.
safetyNotes: Avoid skin contact with DPD reagent.

title: Turbidity — Nephelometric Method
equipment: Formazin or StablCal standards for calibration
steps: Verify instrument calibration with known standards; recalibrate if out of tolerance.
Gently invert the sample to homogenize without introducing air bubbles.
Wipe the sample cell with a lint-free cloth and apply optical coupling fluid/silicone oil if required by the instrument.
Insert the cell into the instrument and read turbidity in NTU.
Take multiple readings and average if the reading is unstable.

title: pH — Electrometric Method
steps: Calibrate the meter using at least two buffers that bracket the expected sample pH.
Rinse the probe with distilled water between buffers and samples.
Immerse the probe in the sample, gently stir, and allow the reading to stabilize.
Record the pH and sample temperature (pH is temperature-dependent).
Rinse and store the probe per manufacturer instructions (typically in storage solution, not dry).

title: Total Dissolved Solids — Conductivity/Gravimetric
equipment: Drying oven and evaporating dish (gravimetric method)
steps: Quick estimate: measure sample conductivity and apply the site-specific conversion factor using the TDS calculator.
Gravimetric (reference) method: filter a measured sample volume through a glass fiber filter.
Evaporate the filtrate in a pre-weighed dish and dry at 180°C to constant weight.
Calculate TDS (mg/L) from the weight gain divided by the sample volume.
Periodically verify the conductivity conversion factor against the gravimetric result.
safetyNotes: Use oven mitts and let dishes cool in a desiccator before weighing.

title: Jar Test Procedure
steps: Fill each jar with an equal volume of raw water sample.
Add increasing coagulant doses to each jar (e.g. one control + 4-6 test doses).
Rapid mix (~100 rpm) for 1 minute to disperse coagulant.
Slow mix (~20-30 rpm) for 15-20 minutes to promote floc formation.
Let settle undisturbed for 30 minutes.
Record floc appearance and measure supernatant turbidity for each jar.
Enter dose/turbidity pairs into the Jar Test calculator to identify the optimum dose.
safetyNotes: Follow the coagulant/polymer SDS for handling precautions.

title: Chemical Feed Pump Calibration
steps: Close the suction valve from the day tank and open the calibration column valve so the pump draws from the graduated column.
Record the starting liquid level in the column.
Run the pump for a measured time interval (e.g. 1-3 minutes) at the current stroke/speed setting.
Record the ending liquid level and calculate the volume drawn down.
Convert the drawdown volume and time into a feed rate, and compare to the target rate from the Feed Pump Rate calculator.
Adjust stroke length/speed and repeat until the measured rate matches the target.
safetyNotes: Wear appropriate PPE for the chemical in use.
